pxe-lab-server.name: PXE lab server (Ubuntu 24.04 cloud image: dnsmasq, iPXE, nginx, NAT)
pxe-lab-server.notes: The network-boot server of the pxe-lab (vms/labs/pxe-lab/): dnsmasq answers DHCP and TFTP on the lab segment pxe-lan (172.20.9.0/24) and nowhere else, iPXE is chained to pxelinux and its menu, nginx serves the Debian 13 installer's kernel and initrd and the answers vmctl writes for each install, and NAT is the segment's only way to the Debian mirror. ~/setup-pxe-server.sh builds all of it and is also the reset. Ported from qlab's pxe-lab (the LAN moved from 192.168.100.0/24, which vmctl link uses, to 172.20.9.0/24).

pxe-lab-client.name: PXE lab client (empty disk, Debian 13 installed over the network)
pxe-lab-client.notes: The diskless machine of the pxe-lab (vms/labs/pxe-lab/): no ISO and no installer of its own. vmctl bootstrap-netboot starts pxe-lab-server if needed, writes this machine's d-i answers into the server's web root and boots the client from its pxe-lan NIC: QEMU's iPXE ROM asks dnsmasq for an address, chains pxelinux over TFTP, the menu loads the Debian 13 installer over HTTP and the installer reaches the mirror through the server's NAT. The second NIC (QEMU's NAT) is how the host logs in afterwards; BOOTIF keeps the installer on the NIC that netbooted.

netboot_config.ready_command: systemctl is-active --quiet dnsmasq nginx pxe-lab-nat && ip -4 addr show pxe-lan | grep -q 172.20.9.1/

late_commands:
for n in /sys/class/net/*; do i=${n##*/}; [ "$i" = lo ] && continue; grep -qs "^iface $i " /etc/network/interfaces || printf '
allow-hotplug %s
iface %s inet dhcp
' "$i" "$i" >> /etc/network/interfaces; done

post_install_run: for i in $(seq 30); do ip -4 -br addr | grep -q ' 172\.20\.9\.' && exit 0; sleep 2; done; exit 1
